title: Believe It or Not?
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. A post can be shared thousands of times in one hour. Sometimes the news is not true. This is called fake news. Fake news can make people believe things that did not happen.

Maria saw a post that said a famous singer was sick. She did not check other sites, and she shared it with her friends. Later, she learned the story was false. Now Maria checks a story on two trusted news sites before she shares it.

questions.text: How often do many people read news on social media?
What did Maria do before she shared the post?
options: She did not check other sites

questions.text: Why is it important to check a story before sharing it?
options: Because fake news can make people believe things that are not true
Because posts are always too short
Because famous singers never get sick
Because sharing takes too much time

questions.text: What does the end of the passage suggest about Maria?
options: She does not use social media
She works for a news site

vocabulary.definition: a message or picture that someone puts on social media
sent or showed something to other people
believed to be reliable and honest

paragraph_translations: Muchas personas leen noticias en las redes sociales todos los días. Una publicación puede compartirse miles de veces en una hora. A veces la noticia no es verdad. Esto se llama noticia falsa. Las noticias falsas pueden hacer que la gente crea cosas que no pasaron.

María vio una publicación que decía que un famoso cantante estaba enfermo. No revisó otros sitios y lo compartió con sus amigos. Después, supo que la historia era falsa. Ahora María revisa una historia en dos sitios de noticias de confianza antes de compartirla.
